chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from some of our companions, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a piece is cut from a man, then it is a dead part. So if a person touches it, then everything in which there is a bone, ghusl becomes obligatory upon the one who touches it. But if there is no bone in it, then no ghusl is upon him.

key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath that becomes obligatory in this case
key_terms.عَظْمٌ: bone, whose presence determines the ruling here
key_terms.قِطْعَةٌ: a severed piece or part cut from the body
key_terms.مَيِّتَةٌ: treated as dead flesh in legal ruling

ai.seo_question: When does touching a severed human body part make ghusl obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a severed human body part. It states that a detached part is treated as a dead part, and touching it necessitates ghusl if it contains bone; if it does not contain bone, then ghusl is not required.
